text: 40了，有各种体会。
en: At 40, I have all sorts of realisations.

text: 我算一直不太迷茫，一直有目标。
en: I'd say I've never been very lost, and have always had goals.

text: 没有大目标，也有小小目标。
en: No grand goals, but I've had little ones too.

text: 30岁的目标是房子，车子，妻子，孩子，帽子（博士帽，官帽）。
en: My goals at 30 were a house, a car, a wife, children, and hats (a doctoral hat, an official's hat).

text: 没能如期实现，但继续奋斗，38岁都实现了。
en: I didn't achieve them on schedule, but kept striving, and by 38 I'd achieved them all.

text: 对未来迷茫，往往是看不清自己的目标。
en: Being lost about the future usually means you can't see your own goals clearly.

text: 而目标不仅和欲望有关，而且和你的能力有关。
en: And goals relate not only to desire, but also to your ability.

text: 若你能力大于欲望，则不会太迷茫。
en: If your ability exceeds your desire, you won't be too lost.

text: 提高能力，降低欲望。
en: Improve your ability, lower your desire.

text: 另外，找鼓励自己的人，找夸自己的人。
en: Also, find people who encourage you, and find people who praise you.

text: 有时你自己发现不了自己的能力，需要别人发现你的能力。
en: Sometimes you can't discover your own ability; you need others to discover it for you.

text: 真心夸你的人就是发现了你的优点和能力。
en: Those who sincerely praise you are the ones who have discovered your strengths and ability.

text: 这个夸你的人往往是你的父母家人，或你的长辈老师，或你的领导大哥。
en: This person who praises you is often your parents and family, or your elders and teachers, or your boss and big brother.

text: 这些人就是你的贵人。
en: These people are your benefactors.

text: 一定要珍惜贵人，珍惜眼前人，感谢命运，感谢自己。
en: Be sure to treasure your benefactors, treasure those close at hand, give thanks for destiny, and give thanks to yourself.

text: 控制自己能控制的，放开自己不能控制的，有智慧区分哪些自己能控制，哪些自己不能控制。
en: Control what you can control, let go of what you cannot, and have the wisdom to distinguish what you can control from what you cannot.

text: 比如有人家里有钱，有人家里没钱，这就是自己不能控制的，不要责备父母，要接受事实继续奋斗继续前进，而不是天天抱怨自己出身不好，抱怨有用的话，世上还会有困难吗？
en: For example, some are born into wealth and others into poverty; this is beyond your control. Don't blame your parents; accept the facts and keep striving and moving forward, rather than complaining every day about your poor background. If complaining worked, would there still be difficulties in this world?

text: 要有耐心，降低需求。
en: Be patient, and lower your needs.

text: 先求生存，先活着，即健康。
en: First seek survival — first, to live, which means health.

text: 再求温饱，即衣食。
en: Then seek food and clothing, that is, sustenance and dress.

text: 第三求小康，即房子和车子，即住行。
en: Third, seek a comfortable living, that is, a house and a car, meaning shelter and transport.

text: 这些都基本上是一个人的目标，成了，可以自主，即做自己的主人。
en: These are basically one person's goals. Once achieved, you can be autonomous, that is, be your own master.

text: 若有关系能力，则谈恋爱，结婚，开公司。
en: If you have the ability to build relationships, then you can court, marry, and start a company.

text: 当一家之主，或一公司之主。
en: Become the head of a family, or the head of a company.

text: 所有这一切，关键是找到看见自己的人，看见自己的优点的人，包容自己缺点的人。
en: The key to all this is to find people who see you, who see your merits, and who accept your shortcomings.

text: 如果找不到这样的人，就自己看见自己，自己鼓励自己，自己包容自己。
en: If you can't find such people, then see yourself, encourage yourself, and accept yourself.

text: 这些目标是分层次的，不要想着全满足，全达到。
en: These goals are hierarchical; don't expect to satisfy or achieve them all.

text: 根本还是前面说的，看自己的能力。
en: Fundamentally, as said before, it comes down to your own ability.

text: 能力强，可以目标高，目标多。
en: If your ability is strong, you can aim high and have many goals.

text: 能力弱，就活着，好死不如赖活着。
en: If your ability is weak, just survive; a miserable life is better than a good death.

text: 我有位老领导，他35岁就成了大型上市公司副总经理，45岁时他辞职下海创业，很快公司做得风生水起。
en: I had an old leader who, at 35, became deputy general manager of a large listed company; at 45 he resigned to start his own business, and soon his company was thriving.

text: 有一次，我外出办事，顺便去他公司去坐坐，聊着聊着就聊到了为人处世这个话题上，我知道老领导在这方面非常厉害，他辞职的时候，董事长、总经理反复做工作，就是为了挽留他，以至于他离职了很久，公司还流传着他的传说。
en: Once, when I was out on business, I dropped by his company for a chat. As we talked, we drifted onto the subject of how to conduct oneself in the world. I knew my old leader was very accomplished in this regard. When he resigned, the chairman and the general manager repeatedly tried to talk him round, all to retain him — so much so that long after he left, stories about him still circulated in the company.

text: 这次聊天时，我的职场之路比较迷茫，所以想和老领导聊聊，请老领导帮忙指点迷津，问他有没有什么技巧？
en: During this conversation, my career path was quite uncertain, so I wanted to chat with my old leader and ask him to help point me in the right direction, and I asked whether he had any techniques?

text: 当我表达完来意后，老领导吸了口烟，说道：你是我的老部下，做人也较实在，我就点拨点拨你！
en: After I explained my purpose, my old leader took a drag of his cigarette and said: 'You were my old subordinate, and you're an honest person, so let me give you a little guidance!'

text: 我赶紧表态说：老领导，您请讲，我洗耳恭听！
en: I quickly responded: 'Old leader, please go ahead, I'm all ears!'

text: 老领导笑了笑说：在我看来，做人也好，做官也罢，只要你做到以下这六条，保证能让你受益终身。
en: The old leader smiled and said: 'In my view, whether you're an ordinary person or an official, as long as you follow these six principles, I guarantee they'll benefit you for life.'

text: 一、记住该记的。
en: One: remember what should be remembered.

text: 很多人总犯一个毛病，那就是丢三落四、撂爪就忘，这是做人的大忌，在职场中该记住什么？
en: Many people always make one mistake: they're scatterbrained and forget things the moment they set them down. This is a great taboo in being a person. What should one remember in the workplace?

text: 一是领导的指示，二是自己布置的工作，三是对下属、合作伙伴、朋友的承诺。
en: First, the leader's instructions; second, the work you've assigned; third, the promises you've made to subordinates, partners, and friends.

text: 二、说对该说的。
en: Two: say what ought to be said, and say it right.

text: 说话是一门艺术，话说对了事情就成了，该说的一定要说，但也不能乱说，核心要把握好一个字：对！
en: Speaking is an art. Get your words right and matters are settled. You must say what needs saying, but you can't speak carelessly either; the crux is grasping one word: right!

text: 什么是对？
en: What is 'right'?

text: 关键要考虑说话的对象、时机、技巧、语气和氛围。
en: The key is to consider the audience, timing, technique, tone, and atmosphere of what you say.

text: 三、干好该干的。
en: Three: do well what ought to be done.

text: 在任何一个组织，靠耍嘴皮子是不能长久生存的，有的领导喜欢听奉承话，但如果换一个领导呢？
en: In any organisation, you cannot survive for long by mere talk. Some leaders like to hear flattery, but what if a different leader comes along?

text: 这就难说了，所以工作一定要干好，这是你在单位立足的前提。
en: That's hard to tell, so you absolutely must do your job well — that's the prerequisite for standing your ground in your workplace.

text: 四、管紧该管的。
en: Four: tightly manage what ought to be managed.

text: 这句话从三个方面去理解，一是管好自己的欲望，不该碰的别碰；二是管好自己的亲属，不该做的别做；三是管好自己的下属，不该犯的错千万别犯。
en: This is understood from three aspects: first, manage your own desires — don't touch what you shouldn't; second, manage your own relatives — don't do what you shouldn't; third, manage your own subordinates — never make the mistakes you shouldn't.

text: 五、摸准该摸的。
en: Five: accurately gauge what should be gauged.

text: 这个摸是让你摸准基层的情况，你不要曲解，作为一个领导最难的是什么？
en: This 'gauging' means getting an accurate read on the situation at the grass roots; don't misinterpret it. As a leader, what is the hardest thing?

text: 绝对是拍板决策，想要正确决策，就不能太懒，要做深入细致调查研究。
en: It is absolutely decision-making. To make correct decisions, you cannot be too lazy; you must conduct in-depth, careful investigation and research.

text: 六、扛起该扛的。
en: Six: bear what must be borne.

text: 做人什么最重要？
en: What is most important in conducting oneself?

text: 绝对是责任，有些人为什么缺少朋友？
en: It is absolutely responsibility. Why do some people lack friends?

text: 有些领导为什么下属不服？
en: Why do some leaders find their subordinates won't submit to them?

text: 因为没有责任和担当，好处是自己的，责任是别人的，谁还跟你玩呢？
en: Because they have no sense of responsibility or accountability: the benefits are their own, the responsibility belongs to others — who would still want to associate with them?

text: 老领导说完之后，笑眯眯的看着我，等我慢慢消化，我琢磨良久才说道：实在是高！
en: After my old leader finished, he watched me with a smile, waiting for me to take it in slowly. I mulled it over for a long time before saying: 'That is truly masterful!'

text: 不过，我没好意思深问，免得领导笑话我没有悟性。
en: Still, I was too embarrassed to ask further, for fear the leader would mock me for lacking understanding.

text: 直到前几天，老领导乔迁新居，我们几个老部下去去他家做客，参观书房的时候，看到书橱里满满都是书，桌子上还放着一套金锋写的《职场避坑指南》，这套书翻阅的痕迹很重，老领导做了不少笔记。
en: Until a few days ago, when my old leader moved into a new home, a few of us old subordinates went to visit him. While touring his study, we saw the bookcase full of books, and on the desk lay a set of 'Workplace Pitfall Avoidance Guide' written by Feng Jin. The set showed heavy signs of use, and my old leader had made many notes in it.

text: 老领导看到我对《职场避坑指南》比较感兴趣，对我说道：我推荐你看看金锋写的《职场避坑指南》，这套书内容有处世谋略、人性心理、口才沟通、做人智慧，让你懂人性、懂人心、通人情，这本书的内容非常实用，每读一遍都会有新的收获，能够让你在职场中会说话、会办事、会做人，我建议你一定要看看。
en: Seeing my interest in 'Workplace Pitfall Avoidance Guide', the old leader said to me: 'I recommend you read Workplace Pitfall Avoidance Guide by Feng Jin. This set covers strategies for dealing with the world, human psychology, eloquence and communication, and the wisdom of being a person. It helps you understand human nature, understand people's hearts, and grasp social bonds. The content is highly practical; every time you read it you gain new insights, and it enables you to speak well, handle affairs well, and conduct yourself well in the workplace. I suggest you really should read it.'

text: 人到中年后，我发现存钱是中年人的最大底气。
en: After reaching middle age, I realised that saving money is a middle-aged person's greatest source of confidence.

text: 年轻的时候，我基本每个月都是月光族，喜欢什么买什么。
en: When I was young, I was basically someone who spent my whole salary every month, buying whatever I liked.

text: 但是如今，家里孩子上下学，还有车贷、房贷、赡养老人，所以经济负担比较重。
en: But nowadays, with the children going to and from school, plus car loans, a mortgage, and supporting the elderly, the financial burden is fairly heavy.

text: 所以，我现在就开始了“死抠硬攒”的生活，用2年的时间存够了15万。
en: So I began living a life of 'scraping and scrimping', and in two years saved up 150,000.

text: 我身边不少朋友，看到我的存钱妙招，都觉得很厉害。
en: Quite a few friends around me, seeing my money-saving tricks, found them really impressive.

text: 今天就把我的存钱妙招分享出来，大家也可以学起来。
en: Today I'll share my money-saving tricks, and everyone can learn them too.

text: 01、做饭
en: 01. Cooking

text: 以前总觉得自己做饭很麻烦，需要买菜、洗菜、切菜、炒菜，吃完饭之后，还需要清洁餐具。
en: I used to think cooking for myself was a hassle: you have to buy vegetables, wash them, chop them, stir-fry them, and after eating you still have to clean the dishes.

text: 不仅过程麻烦，而且每天吃什么、做什么饭，光是想想就很麻烦了。
en: Not only is the process troublesome, but deciding what to eat and what to cook each day is exhausting just to think about.

text: 但是自从有孩子开始，基本一日三餐都是自己做。
en: But ever since having a child, basically all three meals a day are homemade.

text: 这么做，不仅是因为吃着有营养，也是为了省钱。
en: The reason for doing this is not only that it's nutritious, but also to save money.

text: 以前点个外卖，一天就需要上百块，现在自己做饭，一周的菜钱还不到一百。
en: Before, ordering takeaway cost over a hundred yuan a day; now cooking for myself, a week's grocery bill is under a hundred.

text: 所以，省钱、存钱第一步，就是自己做饭！
en: So the first step to saving and storing money is to cook for yourself!

text: 02、不乱买衣服
en: 02. Don't buy clothes indiscriminately

text: 我家基本都不乱买衣服，我、孩子爸爸、孩子的衣服基本有几套穿就足够了。
en: In my family we basically don't buy clothes indiscriminately; my clothes, the children's father's clothes, and the children's clothes — a few outfits each are enough.

text: 尤其是孩子，孩子本身就长得快，衣服新的穿几次就小了。
en: Especially the children — they grow fast, and new clothes become too small after just a few wears.

text: 我家孩子现在穿的衣服，基本都是亲朋好友家孩子穿小的。
en: The clothes my children wear now are basically hand-me-downs from the children of relatives and friends.

text: 自从开始不乱买衣服，真的很省钱。
en: Since we stopped buying clothes carelessly, we've really saved money.

text: 03、不囤货
en: 03. Don't stockpile

text: 我发现，现在很多家庭都特别喜欢囤货，但是我家很少囤货。
en: I've noticed many households nowadays especially like to stockpile, but my family rarely does.

text: 以前觉得囤货比较省钱，毕竟一次性买很多东西，价格便宜。
en: I used to think stockpiling saved money, since buying a lot at once is cheaper.

text: 但是真的囤了很多物品后，家里的面积不仅缩小了，而且还很容易过期。
en: But after actually hoarding many items, not only did the living space shrink, but things also easily expired.

text: 所以现在我基本不囤货，不管什么物品，用完了之后再去买。
en: So now I basically don't stockpile; whatever the item, I buy it after I've used it up.

text: 04、不办卡、不充值
en: 04. No membership cards, no top-ups

text: 我老公基本每个月都要剪一次头发，所以我就给他办了一张理发卡，正好就在我家楼下。
en: My husband gets his hair cut about once a month, so I bought him a hairdresser's card, just downstairs from our flat.

text: 充了500块钱，本来想着能用大半年时间，也不用每次都付钱，还便宜，挺划算的。
en: I topped it up with 500 yuan, thinking it would last over half a year, save us paying each time, and be cheaper — quite a bargain.

text: 但是没想到，剪了两三次头发，理发店就倒闭了。
en: But unexpectedly, after just two or three haircuts, the hairdresser's closed down.

text: 现在卡里还有钱，可是也没人管，就相当于钱打水漂了。
en: Now there's still money left on the card, but no one's around to honour it, so it's effectively money down the drain.

text: 我现在基本不管是剪头发，还是干什么都不会办卡，直接选择团购，价格更便宜。
en: Now I basically never get a card, whether for haircuts or anything else; I just choose group-buying directly, which is cheaper.

text: 05、做副业
en: 05. Take on a side business

text: 大家不管是什么工作，都可以找一些副业来做。
en: Whatever your job, everyone can find some side work to do.

text: 我之所以能存住钱，不仅仅是因为生活中比较节省，还是因为我会利用闲暇时间做一些副业。
en: The reason I can save money is not only that I'm fairly frugal in daily life, but also that I use my spare time to do some side work.

text: 我每天开车上班，下班的时候，会顺路拉一些住我家附近的同事。
en: I drive to work every day, and on the way home I give colleagues who live near me a lift.

text: 刚开始我还不好意思要钱，但是同事们说，不要钱不坐我的车了。
en: At first I was too embarrassed to take money, but the colleagues said they wouldn't ride with me if I didn't.

text: 现在每个月开车的油钱，基本都被同事们平摊掉了。
en: Now the monthly petrol costs of driving are basically shared among the colleagues.

text: 还会利用自己的特长，做一些兼职，比如网上有一些手工类的兼职，一个月下来也能赚一两千元。
en: I also use my own skills to do some part-time work; for example, there are handcraft-type part-time jobs online that can earn one or two thousand yuan a month.

text: 06、拒绝一次性花销
en: 06. Refuse disposable spending

text: 我发现，现在很多人都喜欢一次性花销。
en: I've noticed many people nowadays like disposable spending.

text: 一次性花销，看起来省钱，实际上缺点很多。
en: Disposable spending seems to save money, but actually has many drawbacks.

text: 一次性物品属于消耗品，基本只能用一次，别提多浪费了。
en: Disposable items are consumables; basically they can only be used once — unbelievably wasteful.

text: 我现在为了省钱，一样东西，都会物尽其用，根本不浪费。
en: Now, to save money, I make the most of everything and waste nothing at all.

text: 就连平时装水的水桶，水喝完了，水桶也不会扔掉，直接把前端剪掉，然后放在家里放垃圾桶。
en: Even the water bucket I normally use for water — once the water's finished, I don't throw the bucket away; I simply cut off the top and use it as a bin at home.

text: 07、适当运动
en: 07. Moderate exercise

text: 人到中年后，保持身体健康很重要，不少人可能会去健身房办卡。
en: After middle age, staying healthy is important; many people may go to the gym and take out a membership card.

text: 不过健身房办卡不仅价格贵，而且坚持不下来的话，充的钱可能就浪费了。
en: But a gym membership is not only expensive, and if you can't keep it up, the top-up money may be wasted.

text: 我运动，基本都是跑跑步、跳跳绳，坚决不多花一分钱。
en: For exercise, I basically just run and skip rope, firmly refusing to spend an extra penny.

text: 写在最后：
en: In conclusion:

text: 人到中年，我才发现，存款才是一个人最大的底气！
en: Only in middle age did I realise that savings are a person's greatest source of confidence!

text: 若你也想存钱，不如学学我这些抠搜的存钱妙招。
en: If you also want to save money, you might as well learn my penny-pinching saving tricks.
